label: Delimiter step when the first original token (the first to be recalled) is one of d,k,v,b,3,m,e,w,s (also h,x,l,r)
explanation: Mainly a delimiter-step unit: 77% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step (40% of delimiter steps fire), and it essentially never fires in the original phase. Whether it fires at <DEL> depends on which token is output there, i.e. orig(0). Precision by first token: d 0.96, k 0.91, v/b 0.87, 3 0.82, m 0.81, e/w 0.77, s 0.68, then a weaker tier h/x/l/r at 0.53-0.59. It almost never fires for a/c/g/i/j/n/y or the digits 0/1/2. The largest activations (near max) are <DEL> steps with first token d or b. The other ~22% of mass is weak and diffuse firing early in the copy phase (recall_idx 1-2), enriched when the input is i/0/j/c and when the output is in the same token set. Adding that as a clause only nudges F1 from 0.60 to 0.61, so it is left out. Dev F1 0.60, mass recall 0.69.
